IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.   3626   OF 2026
(@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRIMINAL) NO. 6286/2026)
RANJEET SINGH ALIAS RAJA      APPELLANT(S)
VERSUS
STATE OF RAJASTHAN & ORS.       RESPONDENT(S)
ORDER
1. We have heard learned counsel for the appellant,
learned counsel for the respondent-State of Rajasthan and
learned counsel for Respondent No.3-de facto complainant.
2. Leave granted.
3. The appellant is aggrieved by order dated 23.03.2026
passed by the High Court of Rajasthan at Jodhpur (briefly
the ‘High Court’ hereinafter), rejecting the prayer for
anticipatory bail of the appellant.
4. It is stated that appellant has been arrayed as an
accused in FIR No.115/2025 registered at Police Station-
Lalgarh  Jatan,  District-  Ganganagar,  Rajasthan  under
Sections 126(2), 115(2) and 189(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya
Sanhita, 2023 (for short, ‘BNS’).
5. Allegation against the appellant is that he had
caused injury to the de facto complainant.
6. This Court, by order dated 13.04.2026, had issued
notice and granted interim protection to the appellant
1

--- Page 454 ---
subject  to  the  appellant  co-operating  with  the
investigation.
7. Learned counsel for the respondent-State of Rajasthan
has drawn the attention of the Court to the counter
affidavit filed and submits that appellant has number of
criminal  antecedents.  That  apart,  the  present  case
concerns  causing  of  bodily  injury  to  the  de  facto
complainant.  Therefore,  appellant  may  not  be  granted
anticipatory bail.
8. Submission of learned counsel for the respondent-
State of Rajasthan is supported by learned counsel for
Respondent No.3-the de facto complainant, who submits that
in a case of this nature, anticipatory bail may not be
granted to the appellant.
9. On the other hand, learned counsel for the appellant
has drawn the attention of the Court to the rejoinder
affidavit filed by the appellant and submits that in one
case, appellant has been acquitted whereas trial in the
other cases are ongoing, where appellant has been enlarged
on bail. In a case relating to the Illegal Gambling Act,
appellant was convicted and only sentence of fine was
imposed. He submits that pursuant to the order of this
Court dated 13.04.2026, appellant has been co-operating
with the investigation.
10. This fact is not denied by learned counsel for the
respondent(s).
11. Considering the above, we are of the view that the
2

--- Page 455 ---
interim protection granted by this Court vide order dated
13.04.2026 should be made absolute.
12. That being the position, we set aside the impugned
order dated 23.03.2026 passed by the High Court and make
the  order  dated  13.04.2026  absolute.  However,  the
appellant  shall  continue  to  co-operate  with  the
investigation of the case.
13. We make it clear that in the event appellant does not
co-operate with the investigation or tries to influence
the witnesses, the respondent-State of Rajasthan would be
at liberty to move for cancellation of bail.
14. Consequently, the Criminal Appeal is allowed.
15. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.
…………………………………………………...J.
      
   [UJJAL BHUYAN]
…………………………………………………...J.
     [ATUL S. CHANDURKAR]
NEW DELHI;
03rd AUGUST, 2026.

    IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA    
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO. 9145 OF 2012
NARAYAN SINGH(D) THROUGH LRS.                 APPELLANT(S)
                                VERSUS
SH. BHULLE (DEAD) THROUGH LRS.                RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R 
1. The appellant(s) challenge the judgment and order dated
09.08.2012 passed by the High Court of Delhi in L.P.A.No.333 of
2005 titled “Bhule vs. Narayan Singh (deceased) & Anr.”.
2. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties we are of
the considered view that no interference is warranted in the
well-reasoned judgment of the High Court which has, in our
considered  view,  correctly  interpreted  the  provisions  of
Sections 48, 51 and 53 of the Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954 (for
short “the Act”). The High Court correctly held that upon the
death of a female, the holding shall devolve upon the legal
heirs in terms of Section 53 of the Act and not upon the nearest
surviving heir of the last male proprietor, as is so provided
under  Section  51  (2)(a)(i).   The  High  Court  correctly
interpreted that such right would flow and devolve in terms of
Section 51 (2) (a) (ii) and not Section 51 (2)(a)(i).
1

--- Page 476 ---
3. In view of the above, we find no merit in the present
appeal.  The same stands accordingly dismissed.
4. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO(s).  507 OF 2015  
THE STATE OF WEST BENGAL & ORS.                    APPELLANT(S)
                                VERSUS
DIPAK SUBBA                                        RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. The appellants challenge the judgment/order dated
13.08.2013 in WPST No.301 of 2013 passed by the High
Court of Calcutta.
2. As  per  the  Office  Report  dated  28.07.2026,
alternative arrangement notice on the sole respondent is
complete, but none has entered appearance, perhaps for
the reason that with the passage of time, the respondent
would have lost interest, since the impugned order dated
13.08.2013 passed in his favour was stayed by this Court
vide order dated 07.10.2013.
3. From the order passed by the Tribunal rejecting the
appellants'  claim,  it  is  evident  that  criminal
proceedings stood initiated against the respondent for
having forged documents, in particular the school leaving
certificate, which formed part of the selection process
for the post of constable. The High Court took the view
that  unless  proven  otherwise,  the  presumption  of
innocence operates in favour of the candidate, and as
1

--- Page 485 ---
such, he was entitled to consideration for appointment to
the post of constable.
4. We are of the considered view that the High Court
fell into error, more so when, as has emerged from the
record, a chargesheet stood filed against the respondent,
for having committed the crime, with regard to the very
same  document  based  on  which,  he  was  seeking  his
appointment.
5. In view of the above, the impugned judgment/order
dated 13.08.2013 shall stand set aside.
6. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

(SANJAY KAROL)
..................J.

CIVIL APPEAL NO(s).      OF 2026
(@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CIVIL) NO(s).36074/2025)
NISHA PRAJAPATI & ORS.                             APPELLANT(S)
                                VERSUS
ASHISH MOHAN                                       RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. The appellants challenge the judgment/order dated
25.09.2025 in Appeal from Order No.418/2024 passed by the
High Court of Uttarakhand at Nainital.
3. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the material available on record, we are of the
considered view that both the courts below, that is, the
Trial Court as also the High Court, erred in rejecting
the appellants’ application filed under Order IX Rule 13
of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 seeking setting
aside of ex-parte judgment and decree dated 23.08.2019.
In our considered view, the appellants had made out a
case in support of the plea so taken by them. The delay
was not inordinate, being of merely 30 days, and there
was sufficient explanation by the appellants for not
entering appearance or taking steps in accordance with
law.
4. As such, we quash and set aside the order dated
01.08.2024 in Misc. Case No. 18 of 2019 in Suit No. 134
1

--- Page 491 ---
of  2018  passed  by  the  learned  Civil  Judge  (Senior
Division), Vikasnagar, Dehradun, and the order dated
25.09.2025 in Appeal from Order No.418 of 2024 passed by
the High Court of Uttarakhand at Nainital. Consequently,
the judgment and decree dated 23.08.2019 in Suit No. 134
of 2018 on the file of the Civil Judge (Senior Division),
Vikasnagar, Dehradun is also set aside, and the suit is
restored to its original number.
5. The parties shall appear before the Trial Court on
01.09.2026.
6. The  appellants  undertake  to  file  their  written
statement before the next date of listing before the
Trial Court. The undertaking is accepted and taken on
record.
7. Since the suit is of the year 2018, the Trial Court
shall endeavour to decide the same within a period of one
(01) year from today. The parties undertake to fully
cooperate and not take any unnecessary adjournments.
8. Accordingly, the appeal stands allowed.
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

referred for mediation. As per the report received from the
Supreme Court Mediation Centre, the mediation has failed.

we  are  inclined  to  transfer  the  case  sought  for.  We,
accordingly, allow the transfer petition and direct that the
case bearing No.CS/161091/2025 titled as  "Sarita Sharma vs.
Rashmi Sharma & Ors. ”, pending before the Court of Judicial
Magistrate, Calcutta, be transferred to the competent Court of
Judicial Magistrate, Mathura, Uttar Pradesh.
4. However, if the video conferencing facility is available
with the Court, the benefit of the same shall be extended to
the parties, unless their physical presence is required.
5. The transferor Court shall forthwith transmit the record
of the aforesaid case to the transferee court.

Mr. Arun Poomulli, learned counsel, appearing for the
petitioners  respectively  and  Ms.  Vrinda  Bhandari,

--- Page 500 ---
2
learned Standing Counsel for the State in both the
matters.
2. The  present  petitions  call  in  question  the
correctness  of  the  orders  dated  25-03-2026  in
CRL.OP(MD) Nos. 4115/2025 & 183/2025 passed by the High
Court of Judicature at Madras at Madurai respectively.
By the said orders, the petitioners have been denied
the benefit of bail in connection with FIR No.9/2024
(CC No.76/2025) registered with Police Station NIB-CID,
District Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu,  for the offences
punishable under Sections 8(c), 29(1) & 20(b)(ii)(c) of
the  Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act,
1985 (for shot, ‘NDPS Act’).
3. We  have also  perused the  records including  the
counter affidavit filed by the State. The petitioners
are  in  custody  since  02/03.09.2024.  The  counter
affidavit(s) indicates that chargesheet is filed on
22.02.2025. About 32 witnesses are listed. Admittedly
till date, not a single witness has been examined. The
trial  is  bound  to  take  considerable  time.  The
petitioners have already put in approximately two years
in custody.
4. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of
the case; the fact the chargesheet is filed as early as
on 22.02.2025; that not a single witness has been
examined till date; the likelihood that the trial to
take conclude; and keeping in mind the principle of

--- Page 501 ---
3
Article 21 of the Constitution of India and the twin
condition of Section 37 of the NDPS Act, we are
inclined to enlarge the petitioners on bail.
5. Accordingly, we direct that petitioners shall be
enlarged on bail subject to the satisfaction of the
concerned Trial Court in connection with the aforesaid
FIR/case and for the offences mentioned hereinabove.
6. The Special Leave Petitions are disposed of in the
above terms.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand
disposed of.

and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for
a period of three years and fine of Rs.5,000/- and
in default of payment of fine, simple imprisonment
for one month.

judgment of the Andhra Pradesh High Court dated

SLP (Crl.) D. No.37214/2026 2

of sentence for eight (08) weeks to enable him to

acquitted  by  the  Court  of  II  Addl.  Chief

6. The appellant was exempted from surrendering
vide order dated 17.07.2026 of this Court. On a
prima facie consideration, we are of the opinion
that  this  is  a  fit  case  for  suspending  the

pending final disposal of the appeal.
7. The sentence imposed on the appellant is

1. The petitioner was denied anticipatory bail
by the High Court in connection with FIR No.139 of
2026  dated  18.06.2026  registered  with  Police
Station Bamori, District Guna, Madhya Pradesh for
the offence punishable under Sections 69, 115(2)
and 351(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
(for short “BNS”).
2. The  petitioner,  who  is  SDO,  Forest,  is
accused of having physical relations with the
victim/complainant on the pretext of marriage, as
well as blackmailing her with obscene videos. The
alleged incidents took place while the victim was
working as a cook at the petitioner’s official
bungalow, which engagement is disputed.
3. The impugned order has been challenged by
raising several grounds such as the delay of more
than 1 year & 8 months from the date of alleged
first incident in filing of FIR. Two detailed
SLP (Crl.) No.13808/2026      2

--- Page 534 ---
enquiry reports dated 24.01.2026 and 05.06.2026,
respectively, concluded the complaint to be false.
4. We order that in the event of arrest of the
petitioner  in  connection  with  the  offence
enumerated above, he shall be released on bail,
subject to co-operation in the investigation and
such other terms and conditions the I.O. may deem
fit to impose.
5. Once the petitioner is released on bail by
the I.O., on directions issued by the I.O. or
summons issued by the jurisdictional court, the
petitioner shall appear before the trial court and
furnish fresh bail bonds and ensure due appearance
in the trial.
6. With  the  aforesaid,  this  petition  stands
disposed of.
7. Pending  applications,  if  any,  also  stand
disposed of.

appellant,  the  request  of  the  appellant  for
2

ATUL KUMAR KANSAL & ORS. RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. The appellant, H.D.F.C. Bank Limited, is aggrieved by the
order dated 08.04.2025 passed by the National Company Law
Appellate  Tribunal1 at  New  Delhi,  dismissing  its  Company
Appeal (AT) (Insolvency) No. 549/2025. 
2. The grievance of the appellant-Bank before the NCLAT was that
properties which ought not to have been included in the
Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process of M/s. Universal
Buildwell Private Limited, the corporate debtor, were so
included to its detriment. According to the appellant-Bank,
the corporate debtor had sold 9 commercial units in the
building constructed by it in Gurugram, Haryana, to M/s.
Nayanika Holdings Pvt. Ltd., respondent No. 3, which had
availed loan facilities from the appellant-Bank to facilitate
such acquisition under the security of those units.
3. The appellant-Bank approached the NCLAT apprehending that the
units sold to respondent No.3 would also be included in the
resolution plan of the Successful Resolution Applicant 2, the
1  For short ‘NCLAT’
2  For short ‘SRA’
1

--- Page 599 ---
Consortium of Universal Aura Welfare Association, Universal
Greens Buyers Association and Universal Business Park Owners
Association, viz., respondent No. 2. 
4. However, respondent No. 2 filed a counter affidavit before
this Court wherein, at paragraph 31, it stated that the
property of M/s. Nayanika Holdings Pvt. Ltd., respondent No.
3, had not been included in the resolution plan and the fact
that the properties sold through conveyance deeds had been
excluded from the properties of the corporate debtor had been
recorded in the order of the National Company Law Tribunal,
New Delhi, dated 07.03.2025. 
5. We may also note that the units sold to M/s. Nayanika Holdings
Pvt. Ltd., respondent No. 3, by the corporate debtor are Unit
Nos. 618, 619, 620, 621, 622, 623, 624, 625 and 626 located on
the 6th Floor of Universal Business Park, Sector-66, Village-
Badshahpur, Gurgaon, Haryana. 
6. In the light of the categoric statement made by the SRA in the
counter affidavit, the apprehension of the appellant-Bank now
stands settled. Recording the same, the appeal is disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO.  7052/2023  
H.D.F.C. BANK LTD. APPELLANT(S)
       VERSUS
UMESH AMBIKA PRASAD MISHRA RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. This appeal arises out of the order dated 13.09.2023 passed by
the  National  Consumer  Disputes  Redressal  Commission1,  New
Delhi, in Consumer Case No. 331/2014. 
2. By the said order, the NCDRC rejected the written statement
filed by the appellant-Bank in the said consumer case on the
ground that it was barred by time in terms of the law laid
down by this Court in New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Hilli
Multipurpose Cold Storage Pvt. Ltd.2. 
3. Aggrieved  thereby,  the  appellant-Bank  filed  the  present
appeal. By order dated 10.11.2023, this Court stayed further
proceedings in the consumer case. 
4. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, we find
that the NCDRC failed to take note of a crucial factual
aspect, verification of which stemmed from the law laid down
by this Court in New India Assurance Co. Ltd. (supra). 
5. The aforesaid judgment categorically held that, unless the
notice served upon the opposite party in a consumer case is
1  For short ‘NCDRC’
2  (2020) 5 SCC 757
1

--- Page 602 ---
accompanied by a copy of the consumer case, it would not
amount to proper and adequate service of notice, whereupon the
limitation for filing of a written statement by such opposite
party would commence. 
6. In the case on hand, we find that the NCDRC failed to examine
this aspect by inspecting the record to verify whether the
notice sent in October, 2019, which is stated to have been
served upon the appellant-Bank on 29.10.2019, was actually
accompanied by a copy of the consumer case. 
7. In the absence of this verifiable fact being established
beyond  doubt,  the  NCDRC  ought  not  to  have  rejected  the
appellant-Bank’s written statement, filed within time after
service of a fresh notice in the year 2021 along with a copy
of the consumer case. 
8. The  appeal  is,  accordingly,  allowed,  setting  aside  the
impugned order passed by the NCDRC in Consumer Case No.
331/2014. 
9. The NCDRC shall take on record the written statement filed by
the H.D.F.C Bank Ltd. and consider the matter on its merits
and in accordance with law. 
10. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of. 
..........................J.
(SANJAY KUMAR)
..........................J.
(SANJEEV SACHDEVA)
NEW DELHI;
AUGUST 04, 2026.
2

and requested that the petitioner be directed to pay the

5. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has

today. 
6. In view of the aforesaid, no further orders are
required to be passed in the present case. The criminal
proceedings arising out of C.C. No. 140 of 2020, registered

punishable under Sections 163 and 164 of the Railways Act,

which was forfeited on account of the violation of terms
and conditions of the contract between the parties, shall
not be refunded to the petitioner. However, the criminal

Leave granted.
2. The appellant has been convicted under Sections 302, 34 of the
Indian  Penal  Code,  1860  (IPC)  and  sentenced  to  undergo  life
imprisonment by the T rial Court in connection with FIR No.462 of
2021 registered at Police Station Sukhi Sevaniya, District Bhopal,
Madhya Pradesh. The High Court rejected the appellant’s second
application for suspension of sentence and bail.
3. Circumstantial  evidence  points  towards  the  appellant’s
involvement in the murder of Sunil Namdev, wherein the appellant
along  with  other  co-accused  persons  allegedly  attacked  the
deceased and the injuries sustained turned fatal. The appellant is
alleged to have held the hands of the victim when the others struck
him with weapons.
4. On  a  prima  facie consideration,  we  find  it  appropriate  to
suspend the sentence of the appellant on parity with co-accused

--- Page 632 ---

Court  of  Madhya  Pradesh;  and  co-accused  Mohd.  Waleem  Khan,
whose sentence stands suspended vide order dated 07.05.2026 of
this Court, who are alleged to have committed the overt acts. 
5. We  set aside the order of the High  Court and suspend the
sentence  of  the  appellant  till  the  appeal  is  pending  before  the
Appellate Court. The appellant shall be released on bail on such
conditions the Trial Court may deem fit to impose.
6. The appeal is disposed of.

SHIVA SHAKTI SECURITY SERVICES                     Petitioner(s)

(IA No. 176846/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING C/C OF THE IMPUGNED
JUDGMENT & IA No. 180142/2026 - PERMISSION TO FILE ADDITIONAL
DOCUMENTS/FACTS/ANNEXURES)
 
Date : 04-08-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE J.B. PARDIWALA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE K. VINOD CHANDRAN
For Petitioner(s) :

For Respondent(s) :

                   Mr. Navneet Kumar, Adv.                   
                   
                   Mr. Siddharth Sangal, AOR
                   Ms. Richa Mishra, Adv.
                   Ms. Mrinalini Tandon, Adv.
                   Ms. Kashish Tewatia, Adv.
                   
                   Mr. Shouryabrata Mandal, AOR
    Mr. Orijit Dalmia, Adv.
    Ms. Swati Dalmia, Adv.
    Mr. Shubham Raj, Adv.                   

--- Page 668 ---
2
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The petitioner before us is a provider of security services.
The petitioner was engaged by the official liquidator to guard,
protect and preserve the assets and properties of the company after
the company was ordered to be wound up.
2. It is the case of the petitioner that having rendered such
services continuously for several years and raised invoices from
time to time, the State Bank of India, as one of the secured
creditors, should make the necessary payment towards the services
rendered by the petitioner.
3. The High Court, while dismissing both the appeals preferred by
the petitioner, has observed in para 27 as under:
“Section 529 the Companies Act; 1956 does not assist the
appellant.  Appellant  can  make  its  claim  before  the  NCLT.
Pendency of the claim of the appellant, or its alleged non-
payment does not qualify to hold that, the company petition
attend a irreversible stage warranting the Company Court not to
transfer the winding up petition to the NCLT.”
4. Thus, the High Court has taken the view that Section 529 of
the Companies Act would not come to the aid of the petitioner
before us, however, the petitioner should put forward its claim
before the NCLT.
5. We are informed that over a period of time, the matter has now
reached the stage of CIRP before the NCLT. It shall be open for the
petitioner to join the proceedings before the NCLT and put forward
its claim. 
6. With the aforesaid, this petition stands disposed of. 
7. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
 (VISHAL ANAND)                                    (POOJA SHARMA)

1. Dr. S. Muralidhar, the learned Senior counsel appearing for
the petitioner submitted that the Respondent No.1 was not a

--- Page 684 ---
2
registered enterprise under Section 2(n) of the Micro, Small and
Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act, 2006 when the contract
between the petitioner and the Respondent No.1 came to be entered
into.
2. According to the learned Senior counsel, the Respondent No.1
got itself registered only on 3-8-2020. The application under
Section 18 of the MSMED Act for recovery of certain amounts was
filed on 6-8-2020.
3. In such circumstances, referred to above, according to the
learned Senior counsel, the Facilitation Council under the MSMED
Act had no jurisdiction to entertain the application filed under
Section 18 of the Act by the Respondent and, therefore, the
impugned award could be said to be nullity.
4. According to the learned Senior counsel, the aforesaid issue
is at large before the larger bench of this Court in the matter
titled “NBCC v. State of West Bengal and Others” reported in (2025)
3 SCC 440 (Civil Appeal No.3705/2024).
5. In view of the aforesaid, let this matter be tagged with the
matter which is to be heard by a larger Bench.
6. Interim order to continue.

4. However, this is subject to payment of up-to-date
arrears of maintenance as per the order impugned. We make
it clear that if on or before the next date, the entire
up-to-date  arrears  of  maintenance  is  not  paid,  the
petition shall be dismissed summarily.
5. List on 20.05.2026.”
3. Today, it is not in dispute that nothing has been paid by the
petitioner-husband to the respondent-wife during the interregnum.
4. Having  regard  to  the  aforesaid  and  the  fact  that  on
13.03.2026, the matter was directed to be listed on 20.05.2026 and
since that day also, not even a single rupee being paid to the
respondent-wife  clearly  indicates  that  the  intention  of  the
petitioner-husband is not bona fide.
5. Even otherwise, we have considered the matter on merits and do
not find any infirmity in the impugned order.
6. Accordingly, the present petition stands dismissed.

1

--- Page 1016 ---
Section 5 and 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual
Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 and has been sentenced to
undergo seven years of rigorous imprisonment and life
imprisonment under these Sections.
2. The  case  of  the  prosecution  is  based  on
circumstantial  evidence.  We  have  seen  the  evidence,
particularly the statement of Mohd. Hanif (PW-2), Samarth
(PW-4), and Deepak (PW-5), who had seen the petitioner(s)

morning hours of 19.01.2013.

sister of the prosecutrix, namely Deepa (PW-6), as well as
the first informant, Pooja (PW-7).

imposed upon the appellant requires no interference from
this Court.

dismissed.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. Exemption Applications are allowed.
3. The petitioner, a 21 year old, has been denied regular bail by
the High Court in connection with FIR No.3 of 2025 dated 20.01.2025
registered with the Women Police Station Nahan, District Sirmour,
Himachal Pradesh, for the offence punishable under Sections 65(1),
78 and 137(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (for short
“BNS”) and Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual

--- Page 1080 ---
2
Offenses (POCSO) Act, 2012. The petitioner has been in judicial
custody since 31.01.2025.
4. Based on the complaint registered by the victim’s mother, the
FIR was registered accusing the petitioner of committing rape of a
15 year old girl victim (PW1) with whom he is alleged to have been
in a romantic relationship. 
5. A  charge-sheet  was  filed  on  16.03.2025  followed  by  a
supplementary  charge-sheet  dated  03.06.2025.  The  prosecution
opposed grant of bail as only 3 or 4 witnesses remain to be
examined by the trial court.
6. On a prima facie consideration of the fact that the petitioner
has been in custody for 1 year and 7 months, the PW1’s statement
before the trial court denying any sexual relations with the
petitioner,  and  the  SFSL  report  confirming  absence  of  any
incriminating substance, we are of the opinion that the petitioner
can be released on bail, subject to terms and conditions that the
jurisdictional court may deem fit to impose. Ordered accordingly.
7. With the above directions, the Special Leave Petition is
disposed of.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.
